What calibers will you be reloading?

45, 308, and 8mm most likely. I've got a couple of 9mm and an AR, but I don't put enough rounds through them to have much brass laying around.

My goal is to find a good setup for my common rounds, and then stop reloading. I'll just save the brass and budget in supplies with each paycheck. When I need to reload because I can't find ammo, that's when I'll be reloading.

Most important safety habit - store your powder and dies outside of your reloading room, and only bring in one set at a time. This alone, if followed faithfully, will eliminate the most severe hazard. Never leave powder in the hopper either.

If your .308 is a semiauto you'll need to reform the brass down to the base. Lube and carbide dies are your friends.

Take care not to load your 8mm bullets (.323) into the .308(.308).

Cast lead and light charges are great for the 8mm, eliminates wear and tear on you and the gun. Read this:

https://castbulletassoc.org/forum/thread/1387-the-load-is-13-grains-of-red-dot/

Try to select powders that fill the case - this makes errors easy to spot. Watch case length on the .45, it headspaces on the case mouth. Learn how to spot incipient case head failures with a bent paperclip - this is critical with the .308:

https://www.google.com/search?client=safari&rls=en&q=incipient+case+head+failure+paperclip&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8

And never forget The Great Lie: Reloading does not save money! It just lets you shoot more.
